text: A word problem becomes manageable when quantities are named before calculating. A delivery service charges five dollars plus two dollars per kilometer. Let d measure distance in kilometers and c measure the total charge in dollars.
title: Idea 1

text: For a four-kilometer delivery, the variable part is eight dollars, then the fixed fee adds five. The total thirteen dollars includes both contributions. Units prevent mistaking the five-dollar fee for five additional kilometers.
title: Idea 2

text: A nineteen-dollar bill reverses the question. Remove the fixed five-dollar fee to isolate fourteen dollars of distance charges, then divide by two dollars per kilometer. The resulting seven has units of kilometers, matching the unknown we named.
title: Idea 3

text: Finally check the model against the story. Nonnegative distances make the total at least five dollars, so a three-dollar bill cannot fit this pricing rule. A mathematically computed answer may be invalid if it violates the context or its units.
title: Idea 4
